newsitem.title: INDIA: India BHEL exports rise 43 pct in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India BHEL exports rise 43 pct in 96/97.

text.p: India's state-run Bharat Heavy Electrical Ltd (BHEL) said on Thursday it exported equipment worth 12.04 billion rupees ($336 million) in 1996/97 (April-March) compared with 8.42 billion in the previous year.
BHEL makes electrical machinery and power equipment which in 1996/97 went to Greece, Iran, Bangladesh, Malaysia, Japan, Indonesia, Singapore, the United States and Britain.
"Total export turnover during the year at 12.04 billion rupees was an increase of 43 percent over that of 8.42 billion achieved last year," BHEL chairman R.K.D. Shah told a briefing.
Shah said the company was trying to explore new world markets and exports in 1997/98 would substantially increase. "We have identified certain target export markets such as the Gulf."
The company received total orders worth 71.88 billion rupees in 1996/97, out of which export orders were worth 1.4 billion. Its total orders in 1995/96 were 46.82 billion rupees.
BHEL started the new financial year beginning on April 1, with total orders worth 106 billion rupees, a company statement said.
BHEL's net profit rose to 4.68 billion rupees in 1996/97 against 3.50 billion in the previous year. Its earning per share increased to 19.21 rupees from 14.31 rupees.
Gross profit rose to 8.48 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 5.82 billion, the statement said. Its turnover stood at 57.40 billion rupees in 1996/97 compared with 48.33 billion in 1995/96, it added.
Shah said BHEL planned to make capital investments worth 1.5 billion rupees in 1997/98 against 900 million rupees in the previous year.
The company would concentrate on technology upgrading and research and development in 1997/98 to become a "global player."
